source_text: Si ergo incredibile est vel ignorasse apostolos plenitudinem praedicationis vel non omnem ordinem regulae omnibus edidisse, videamus, ne forte apostoli quidem simpliciter et plene, ecclesiae autem suo vitio aliter acceperint quam apostoli proferebant. Omnia ista scrupulositatis incitamenta invenias praetendi ab haereticis. Tenent correptas ab apostolo ecclesias, O insensati Galatae, quis vos fascinavit? et, Tam bene currebatis, quis vos impediit? ipsumque principium, Miror, quod sic tam cito transferimini ab eo qui suos vocavit in gratia, ad aliud evangelium. Item ad Corinthios scriptum, quod essent adhuc carnales, qui lacte educarentur, nondum idonei ad pabulum; qui putarent, se scire aliquid, quando nondum scirent quemadmodum scire oporteret. Cum correptas ecclesias opponunt, credant emendatas. Sed et illas recognoscant de quarum fide et scientia et conversatione apostolus gaudet et deo gratias agit, quae tamen hodie cum illis correptis unius institutionis iura miscent.
thought_title: The heretics' objection from corrected churches
orientation: Tertullian is answering the heretics' claim that the apostles did not teach the full rule of faith to all churches, and now he turns to the heretics' use of Paul's rebukes to certain churches.
pass_a_gloss: If therefore it is unbelievable either that the apostles were ignorant of the fullness of the preaching or that they did not publish the whole order of the rule to all, let us see whether perhaps the apostles indeed taught simply and fully, but the churches by their own fault received otherwise than the apostles were bringing forth. You may find all those incitements of scrupulosity being put forward by the heretics. They hold up the churches rebuked by the apostle: O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you? and, You were running so well, who hindered you? and the very beginning: I wonder that you are so quickly transferred from him who called you in grace to another gospel. Likewise it was written to the Corinthians that they were still carnal, who were being nourished with milk, not yet fit for solid food; who thought that they knew something, when they did not yet know how they ought to know. When they set against us the rebuked churches, let them believe that those churches were corrected. But let them also recognize those churches over whose faith and knowledge and conduct the apostle rejoices and gives thanks to God, which nevertheless today share with those rebuked churches the rights of one institution.

Preserves the abstract noun and the idea of restless over-carefulness that leads to doubt

pass_b_english: If, then, it is unbelievable either that the apostles did not know the fullness of the preaching or that they did not publish the whole order of the rule to everyone, let us consider whether perhaps the apostles did teach simply and fully, but the churches through their own fault received differently from what the apostles were bringing forth. You will find all these incitements of scrupulosity put forward by the heretics. They hold up the churches rebuked by the apostle: "O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you?" (Galatians 3:1), and "You were running so well; who hindered you?" (Galatians 5:7), and the very beginning: "I am astonished that you are so quickly turning away from him who called you in grace to another gospel" (Galatians 1:6). Likewise it was written to the Corinthians that they were still carnal, fed on milk and not yet ready for solid food (1 Corinthians 3:1-2), who thought they knew something when they did not yet know how they ought to know (1 Corinthians 8:2). When they set the rebuked churches before us, let them believe those churches were corrected. But let them also recognize the churches over whose faith and knowledge and conduct the apostle rejoices and gives thanks to God—churches which even today share the rights of one institution with those rebuked ones.

last_rejected.why: Latin says apostles did NOT teach simply and fully; English asserts they did, reversing the meaning.
last_rejected.fix: perhaps even the apostles did not teach simply and fully, but the churches through their own fault received differently from what the apostles were bringing forth.
last_rejected.ruling: Context is hypothetical: 'ne forte...acceperint' = 'lest perhaps the apostles did teach...but the churches received differently.' English correctly renders the subjunctive hypothesis.
